prompt: A recipe uses $2$ cups of flour to make $24$ cookies. At the same rate, how many cups of flour are needed to make $60$ cookies?
hint: The recipe is scaled up at the same rate, so flour and cookies stay in the same ratio. Set up two equal ratios.

hints.text: The recipe is scaled up at the same rate, so flour and cookies stay in the same ratio. Set up two equal ratios.
Write cups over cookies on both sides: $\dfrac{2}{24} = \dfrac{c}{60}$. Cross-multiply and solve for $c$.
Cross-multiplying gives $24c = 120$, so $c = 5$. The recipe needs $5$ cups of flour.

learningObjective: Set up and solve a proportion in context.
explanation: Keep the same units in the same positions: $\dfrac{2}{24} = \dfrac{c}{60}$, with cups on top and cookies on the bottom.
Cross-multiply to remove the fractions: $2(60) = 24c$, so $120 = 24c$.
Divide by $24$ to get $c = 5$, so $5$ cups of flour are needed for $60$ cookies.

alternativeExplanations.title: Find the rate per cookie first
steps: $2$ cups makes $24$ cookies, so one cookie takes $\dfrac{2}{24} = \dfrac{1}{12}$ cup.
The unit-rate route takes one extra step but reads more naturally, and it makes the answer easy to sanity-check.
